title: Agent Certificate v0 Claim and Non-Claim Records
description: The discriminated `Claim | NonClaim` wire union (C1 Ruling 1, binding). The compiler-input rule is structural here: 'verifier=None must compile only to NonClaim; a populated verifier must compile only to Claim.' A ClaimV0 REQUIRES a populated, versioned verifier reference recording PASS; a NonClaimV0 structurally FORBIDS a verifier field. An instance carrying a null/absent verifier on a claim, or any verifier on a non-claim, validates against NEITHER branch — it is rejected outright, which encodes 'rejection, not downgrade' (a failed or missing verifier can never demote a claim into a lower tier or a non-claim record; it makes the record unrepresentable). Tier is a per-claim field, never per certificate. Tier 4 stays in the ClaimTier enum but is unconstructible in v0 (certification_common_v0_schema.json#/definitions/EmittableClaimTierV0). Non-claims are printed records, never implied by absence. Root instance is one ClaimOrNonClaimV0.

ClaimIdV0.description: The complete conditional v0 claim-ID allowlist ('every one conditional, not shippable today'), RECONCILED against the V4 claim-verifier matrix, whose row IDs are CANONICAL on the wire. The C6 reconciled rulings named the set 'B1 · B3 · C1 · D2 · D5 · G1 · G3', but that namespace collides with the matrix's actual index (the rulings' own §0 collision note misdescribed matrix B3). RECONCILIATION TABLE (rulings ID -> matrix row -> wire ID): rulings B1 (ledger integrity, narrow issuer-signed-seal wording) -> matrix B1 -> B1; rulings C1 (artifact-scoped no-unsupported-claims) -> matrix C1 -> C1; rulings D2 (offline zero-Traigent-backend-egress witness) -> matrix D2 -> D2; rulings 'D5' (issuer-signature validity) -> matrix F1 'Issuer signature and attribution' ('D5' is NOT a matrix claim row; the rulings borrowed a locked decision ID) -> F1; rulings G1 (client evidence-manifest commitment) -> matrix G1 -> G1; rulings G3 (co-signer identity) -> matrix G3 -> G3; rulings 'B3' (registry commitment receipt) -> NO matrix row exists (matrix B3 is 'Adverse history captured', a DIFFERENT claim) -> REG1, an explicitly-marked extension ID pending V4-matrix registration — next-evidence item 12 requires the 26-row matrix to reconcile every claim ID before the compiler emits, so a REG1 claim may not print until that registration lands. The raw tokens 'D5' and a registry-receipt reading of 'B3' are rulings-namespace aliases only and are NOT valid wire IDs. ADVERSE HISTORY (matrix B3; amendment A8: 'otherwise the certificate rewards selective omission') is deliberately NOT in this enum and is NOT covered by REG1: C6 Ruling 5 places 'any operational closeout evidence or failure/waiver classification' in the committee-gated adapter tier, so matrix-B3 adverse history is pending committee admission with its own row, verifier, and template — documented here so it is not silently dropped, unprintable today, unrepresentable until admitted (its tier-1 form is also gated on claim B2's declared universe, itself a mandatory NON-claim in v0). B1c and D6a 'were invented by the proposer and are not registered' and MUST NOT be added. Nothing may print an unregistered ID.

NonClaimIdV0.description: The fourteen mandatory printed NON-claims (C6 'Mandatory printed NON-claims (14)'): the eight suspended/absent V4 matrix rows (A3 deployment binding, A4 drift detection, B2 closeout/execution-completeness reconciliation, E2 statistical validity, E3 winner stability, F3 offline verifiability, G2 selective-disclosure proof, H1 criteria epochs) plus the six standing non-claims (NC_* codes). The certificate envelope requires ALL FOURTEEN, in this order, via tuple validation — a certificate printing fewer is schema-invalid.

NonClaimReasonCatalogV0.description: The pinned v0 non-claim sentence catalog (issuer-controlled; the signed semantics bundle binds this file). Renderers print these sentences; the wire record carries only the non_claim_id and reason_template_id. Sentences: A3 = 'This certificate does not state that the certified revision is running in any environment; it makes no deployment-identity or deployment-binding claim.' · A4 = 'No drift monitoring exists for this subject; absence of a drift finding is absence of checking, not evidence of no drift.' · B2 = 'No closeout or execution-completeness reconciliation was performed; a step that was never recorded cannot be detected.' · E2 = 'This certificate makes no statistical claim; statistical selection validity language is suspended product-wide.' · E3 = 'The winner was not re-run; no winner-stability or reproducibility evidence exists.' · F3 = 'This certificate is not yet independently verifiable offline; verification currently requires Traigent-published software and keys.' · G2 = 'No selective-disclosure mechanism exists; anything not printed here is simply absent and its absence is not recorded.' · H1 = 'This certificate does not record whether evaluation criteria changed during the build.' · NC_STEP_CAPTURE = 'No guarantee that every actually executed material step was recorded.' · NC_PRESEAL_RECORDER = 'No defense against a compromised recorder before sealing.' · NC_TIER4_GAPCHECKED = 'No tier-4 or gap-checked claim.' · NC_TARGET_MINIMIZED = 'Target-minimized disclosure is planned, not shipped.' · NC_CURRENT_ONLINE_FREETEXT = 'Current-online mode discloses tuned free-text configuration values.' · NC_BUILD_SESSION_SCOPE = 'The certificate concerns a build session, not the deployed agent.'

VerifierRefV0.description: A populated, versioned verifier reference. `result` is const PASS: a claim whose verifier did not run, or did not pass, has NO representable form — the compiler rejects it (never downgrades it), per the operational definition of 'unsupported' (C6 Ruling 3(ii)). Verifier identity and version are pinned tokens resolved against the signed verifier catalog; a versionless verifier is unrepresentable.

ClaimEvidenceRefsG1V0.description: The exact evidence-reference tuple for printable claim G1: one audit_report_digest and one client_commitment_digest, in either order. The generic evidence-kind vocabulary remains available for non-printable and historical records, but a current v0 G1 claim cannot carry a ledger-entry commitment or any other reference.

ClaimEvidenceRefsD2V0.description: The exact evidence-reference tuple for printable claim D2: one audit_report_digest and one sdk_witness_bundle, in either order. No ledger-entry commitment, duplicate kind, or additional evidence reference is representable.

ClaimV0.description: A printable v0 claim. The payload and template schemas retain the complete registered family for future evolution, but current v0 emission is deliberately limited to substantive D2 and G1 only: B1, C1, F1, and G3 are self-referential because their PASS verifier runs only after the manifest/signature/audit cycle is finalized, and REG1 remains pending registration. ClaimV0 therefore structurally rejects those IDs; their isolated payload/template/audit-row shapes remain available for a later registered release. D2 and G1 are fixed tier 1 and require co-attestation at the envelope. Every printed claim carries a PASS verifier and audit_report_digest evidence reference. No free-text field exists anywhere in this shape.

evidence_refs.description: Bounded evidence references. MUST include at least one evidence_kind=audit_report_digest reference (SCHEMA-1 P1 fix, 2026-08-24) binding this claim to the pre-issuance audit report that supported it (certificate_audit_report_v0_schema.json#/definitions/AuditReportV0) — Draft-07's `contains` expresses 'at least one'; that a printed claim carries EXACTLY one such reference, and that every printed claim in one certificate references the SAME audit_report_digest value, are verifier obligations this array shape cannot itself enforce (exercised by tests/test_agent_certificate_v0_schemas.py's contract-verifier helper, not merely documented).

allOf.description: Conservative v0 unsupported-claims-abstain rule: only D2 and G1 may be emitted as ClaimV0 records. REG1 is pending registration; B1/C1/F1/G3 are withheld until their post-finalization verifier evidence is independently registered.

NonClaimV0.description: A printed NON-claim record: structurally distinct from a claim (C1 Ruling 1, conceded: 'non-claims structurally distinct from claims'). It carries NO verifier field (additionalProperties:false plus an explicit `not` guard make one unrepresentable) and NO tier — a non-claim asserts nothing, so tiering it would be a category error. The rendered sentence comes from the pinned NonClaimReasonCatalogV0; the wire record carries identifiers only.

ClaimOrNonClaimV0.description: The wire union. The record_type consts make the branches disjoint; an empty/absent verifier can only ever be a NonClaimV0, and a populated verifier can only ever be a ClaimV0.

ClaimsArrayV0.description: The bounded claims array shape (SCHEMA-1, 2026-08-24 pre-issuance correction), factored out of agent_certificate_v0_schema.json so the printed certificate's `claims` field and the signed unsigned-manifest's `claims` coverage section (certificate_unsigned_manifest_v0_schema.json#/definitions/UnsignedManifestV0) reference the identical bounded-array type rather than two independently-maintained copies that could silently diverge. Possibly empty, since every v0 claim is conditional. Compiler-checked equality obligation: the manifest's claims section MUST be copied verbatim from the certificate's claims field (never independently re-derived); Draft-07 cannot check this once only manifest_digest crosses.

NonClaimsFixedTupleV0.description: The FOURTEEN mandatory printed NON-claims, tuple-validated in canonical print order (SCHEMA-1, 2026-08-24 pre-issuance correction: factored out of agent_certificate_v0_schema.json for the same single-source-of-truth reason as ClaimsArrayV0 above — the printed certificate's `non_claims` field and the unsigned manifest's `non_claims` coverage section both reference this one tuple type). All fourteen are required; additionalItems:false plus the min/max bounds make omission, addition, and reordering schema-invalid. Non-claims are printed, never implied by absence.
